'''Kari Kaleva Vilonen''' (born 1955) is a Finnish [[mathematician]], specializing in geometric representation theory. He is currently a professor at the [[University of Melbourne]].<ref name="vita">{{cite web|url=https://cpb-ap-se2.wpmucdn.com/blogs.unimelb.edu.au/dist/1/427/files/2020/06/Short_Vilonen_CV_2020.pdf|title=Curriculum Vitae of Kari Vilonen|access-date=July 8, 2020|archive-date=July 10, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200710133022/https://cpb-ap-se2.wpmucdn.com/blogs.unimelb.edu.au/dist/1/427/files/2020/06/Short_Vilonen_CV_2020.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Education ==
He received in 1983 his [[Ph.D]] from [[Brown University]] under [[Robert MacPherson (mathematician)|Robert MacPherson]] with thesis ''The Intersection Homology ''D''-module on Hypersurfaces with Isolated Singularities''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=4464}}</ref>

== Career ==
From 1983 to 1986 was a [[C. L. E. Moore instructor]] at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], on leave in 1984–1985 at the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]] in [[Berkeley, California]]. Afterward, Vilonen was a  Benjamin Pierce Assistant Professor at [[Harvard University]] from 1986 to 1989. From 1989 to 2000 he was a faculty member at [[Brandeis University]], rising to the rank of Professor in 1996.<ref name="vita" /> After that, he was a professor at [[Northwestern University]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.math.northwestern.edu/~vilonen/ |title=Kari Vilonen, Department of Mathematics, Northwestern University |access-date=2018-03-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180519154001/http://www.math.northwestern.edu/~vilonen/ |archive-date=2018-05-19 |url-status=dead}}</ref> and then a professor at the [[University of Helsinki]] from 2010 to 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/node/5455|title=Humboldt researcher award winner coming to MPIM|website=[[Max Planck Institute for Mathematics]]}}</ref> Starting in 2015, Vilonen has been a professor at the University of Melbourne in [[Australia]].

In 2002, with [[Dennis Gaitsgory]] and [[Edward Frenkel]], he proved the geometrical [[Langlands program|Langlands conjecture]] for curves over finite fields.<ref name="Frenkel Gaitsgory Vilonen pp. 367–417">{{cite journal | last1=Frenkel | first1=E. | last2=Gaitsgory | first2=D. | last3=Vilonen | first3=K. | title=On the geometric Langlands conjecture | journal=Journal of the American Mathematical Society | publisher=American Mathematical Society (AMS) | volume=15 | issue=2 | date=31 December 2001 | issn=0894-0347 | doi=10.1090/s0894-0347-01-00388-5 | pages=367–417| doi-access=free }}</ref>

In 2004, Vilonen, [[Mark Goresky]], Dennis Gaitsgory and Edward Frenkel were awarded a multimillion dollar grant from the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency ([[DARPA]]) to work on a project aimed at establishing links between the Langlands program and dualities in quantum field theory. Later, Frenkel wrote, "We felt like we were in uncharted territory: no mathematicians we knew had ever received grants of this magnitude before." The funds were used to coordinate the work of dozens of mathematicians with the goal of making a concerted effort in a significant area of research.<ref name="Frenkel">{{cite web | last=Frenkel | first=Edward | title=Love and Math: The Heart of Hidden Reality | website=Institute for Advanced Study | url=https://www.ias.edu/ideas/2014/frenkel-love-math | access-date=9 August 2020 |date=2014}}</ref>

In 2007, with Ivan Mirković, he published "Geometric Langlands duality and representations of algebraic groups over commutative rings", which proved the geometric Satake equivalence, a geometric version of the [[Satake isomorphism]].<ref name="Mirković Vilonen pp. 95–143">{{cite journal | last1=Mirković | first1=Ivan | last2=Vilonen | first2=Kari | title=Geometric Langlands duality and representations of algebraic groups over commutative rings | journal=Annals of Mathematics | publisher=Annals of Mathematics, Princeton U | volume=166 | issue=1 | date=1 July 2007 | issn=0003-486X | doi=10.4007/annals.2007.166.95 | pages=95–143| doi-access=free | arxiv=math/0401222 }}</ref>

In 2013, Vilonen received a [[Humboldt Prize]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/pls/web/pub_auswahlergebnisse.main?p_lang=en&p_bereich=PUBL-HFP&p_pattern=&p_humboldt_nation=&p_address_country=&p_address_region=&p_address_city=&p_address_uni=&p_host_country=&p_host_region=&p_host_city=&p_host_uni=&p_fgb1=&p_order_by=F&p_button_search=&p_page=1 |title=Prof. Dr. Kari Vilonen {{!}} Humboldt Research Award {{!}} October 2013 {{!}} Archived copy |access-date=2020-08-09 |archive-date=2020-07-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200711230452/https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/pls/web/pub_auswahlergebnisse.main?p_lang=en&p_bereich=PUBL-HFP&p_pattern=&p_humboldt_nation=&p_address_country=&p_address_region=&p_address_city=&p_address_uni=&p_host_country=&p_host_region=&p_host_city=&p_host_uni=&p_fgb1=&p_order_by=F&p_button_search=&p_page=1 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2014, he was awarded a Simons Fellowship from the [[Simons Foundation]].<ref name="Simons Foundation 2012">{{cite web | title=Simons Fellows in Mathematics | website=Simons Foundation | date=19 June 2012 | url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/grant/simons-fellows-in-mathematics/ | access-date=9 August 2020}}</ref>

In 2020, the [[Australian Research Council]] awarded Vilonen an [[Australian Laureate Fellowship]], their highest award to an individual. This five year grant will allow him to address questions about real groups, algebraic objects which describe the basic symmetries occurring in nature.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.arc.gov.au/news-publications/media/funding-announcement-kits/australian-laureate-fellowships-2020/2020-laureate-profile-professor-kari-vilonen|title = 2020 Laureate Profile: Professor Kari Vilonen|date = 6 July 2020}}</ref>

=== Awards and keynote addresses ===
Vilonen was a [[Guggenheim Fellow]] for the academic year 1997/98.<ref name="John Simon Guggenheim Foundation">{{cite web | title=Kari Vilonen | website=John Simon Guggenheim Foundation | url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/kari-vilonen/ | access-date=9 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200708212730/https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/kari-vilonen/ |archive-date=8 July 2020}}</ref> In 1998 he was an Invited Speaker with talk ''Topological methods in representation theory'' at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Berlin]].<ref>{{cite book|author=Vilonen, Kari|chapter=Topological methods in representation theory|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. II|year=1998|pages=595–604|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011696000}}</ref> In 2004 he was elected a member of the [[Finnish Academy of Science and Letters]].
